newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Leung Kee says shareholding may change.
newsitem.headline: Leung Kee says shareholding may change.

text.p: Leung Kee Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday its substantial shareholders were in litigation which might lead to a disposal of some of their stakes in the company.

Leung Kee said Sincere Time Investment Ltd and Wah Yan Property Ltd had issued a writ of summons to require firms including Orcades Holdings Ltd and Clibanus Ltd to sell, mortgage, charge or dispose of 292.31 million company shares, and to repay a loan of HK$32 million made by Wah Yah to Orcades.
The plaintiffs and the defendants are collectively the substantial shareholders of the company, it said.
The 292.31 million shares represent 37 percent of Leung Kee's share capital. Orcades and Clibanus hold 10 percent and 27 percent of the company respectively, the statement said.

"The litigation is pending court hearing and its outcome is uncertain. The board is accordingly not able to determine whether the litigation will result in any change in trhe substantial shareholders of the company and is not currently aware of any such change," it said.
"The board confirms that the management and daily operation of the company currently remain unchanged," it added.
Trading in the company shares which suspended since April 11, resumed on Tuesday. Its shares fell HK$0.02 to HK$0.29 in early trade.
